Multiplying that usable capacity by $12 million per MW gives about $356 billion annually, or $360 billion using 30 GW. The claimed $435 billion is about 22% above the unrounded calculation. This finding concerns the calculation, not whether future compute demand will justify construction.
limitations: The arithmetic accepts the speaker's capacity and pricing assumptions without validating them.

The decisive item is a reproducible calculation from the source's operands, not independent market measurement.

statement.excerpt: Per my own analysis, NVIDIA’s predicted $1 trillion in Blackwell and Vera Rubin GPU sales (by the end of 2027) represents around 40GW of data center capacity, which will, assuming a PUE of 1.35, result in around 30GW of usable capacity. At a cost of around $12 million a megawatt, that works out to around $435 billion in global annual compute revenue to make these data centers necessary.

our_interpretation: Assess the calculation presented on the publication date, not whether NVIDIA will ultimately achieve its sales forecast.
Treat 40 GW as total facility capacity and divide by the stipulated PUE to obtain usable capacity.
Read $12 million per megawatt as an annual revenue requirement because the stated result is annual revenue. The source does not explicitly supply the annual unit.
Test the stated numerical assumptions without assuming that they establish actual commercial necessity.
criteria.support_condition: The sales-to-capacity assumptions are substantiated and the stated capacity, PUE and per-megawatt assumptions yield approximately $435 billion in annual revenue.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The stated arithmetic produces a materially different annual revenue figure, or independently established inputs invalidate a necessary conversion.
